Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a problem, breaking it into smaller versions of the same problem. Every recursive function needs a base case — a simple condition that stops the recursion — otherwise it would call itself forever. Each time the function calls itself, it makes progress toward that base case, which is what eventually lets the recursion stop.
